summary: AccessService is a thin, well-tested domain layer that implements Decisions 3, 5, 10, 11 correctly and matches the tech-spec's Data Models section verbatim (types, interfaces, method signatures diffed field-by-field, no drift). Independently ran `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/service/... -v` in the golang:1.25-alpine container (Go is not installed on the host) — build is clean, all 14 new TestAccessService_* tests plus subtests pass, and the existing 4 TestCostingService_* tests are unaffected. Grepped the whole server tree for RoleAdmin/HasAccess usage: the has_access||role=='admin' rule lives in exactly one place, the unexported hasEffectiveAccess(user UserRecord) helper, called from GetAccessState and CreateRequest — the implementer's claim holds. Interface shape (narrow UserRepository/AccessRequestRepository, ctx first arg, only domain types crossing the boundary) matches costing.go:168-183 exactly. On the flagged design decision — SetAccess deciding whether to call DecideRequest off a GetUser snapshot instead of a fresh read — I agree it's the right call for this task: the constraint isn't just a preference, it's baked into the tests themselves (TestAccessService_SetAccess_Grant/Revoke assert requestRepo.getCalls == 0, i.e. no second read of the request repo is allowed; TestAccessService_SetAccess_NoExistingRequest_DoesNotCallDecideRequest asserts DecideRequest must not fire when the snapshot shows no request). Given AccessRequestRepository.DecideRequest is documented as a no-op on a missing row, the 'obvious' full fix (always call DecideRequest unconditionally) would trivially close the race, but it's explicitly forbidden by that same test. So within Task 2's scope (no DB, no transaction), the snapshot approach is close to forced, not just convenient, and the accompanying comment explains the trade-off honestly rather than hiding it. This already went through one internal test-design review round (commit 804e010) that added exactly this documentation plus getCalls assertions. Two things are worth a maintainer's attention below: a related but undiscussed partial-failure ordering issue, and the fact that the accepted race isn't tracked anywhere outside a code comment.

findings.description: SetAccess performs two sequential repository writes with no rollback: userRepo.SetAccess(granted) first, then (conditionally) requestRepo.DecideRequest(...). If the flag write succeeds but DecideRequest then fails (access.go:194-196), SetAccess returns a wrapped error to the caller — meaning the HTTP layer will almost certainly report a failure (5xx) to the admin — while has_access has already been changed in storage. This is a different failure mode from the GetUser-snapshot race that's already documented: it's not a concurrent-write race, it's this call's own two-phase write not being atomic. There's no test covering 'DecideRequest fails after a successful SetAccess' (accessRequestRepoStub.decideErr exists but no test sets it), so this behavior — flag toggled, error surfaced anyway — is implicit rather than a verified, intended contract. An admin who retries after seeing an error would call SetAccess again, which is idempotent and harmless here, but a caller that treats the error as 'nothing happened' would be wrong.
findings.recommendation: Either add a test asserting the current behavior (flag change is not rolled back on a subsequent DecideRequest failure) so it's a documented, intentional contract rather than an accident of implementation order, or note this explicitly in the existing race comment at access.go:179-185 alongside the GetUser-snapshot trade-off it's adjacent to. No code change needed if the current behavior is accepted — but it should be visible as a decision, not just discoverable by reading the code.

findings.description: The accepted GetUser-snapshot race (a CreateRequest landing between SetAccess's GetUser read and its DecideRequest call leaves a permanently-stale pending access_requests row, since the next CreateRequest from that user will short-circuit to ErrConflict before ever reaching the repository once has_access is true) is well-documented in a code comment, but isn't recorded anywhere a future task-planner would see it without reading access.go line by line — not in tech-spec.md, not in a decisions.md entry for this task. The comment itself correctly points at 'the repository layer, one transaction' as the real fix, which is exactly Task 3/4's territory, but nothing currently routes that follow-up there.
findings.recommendation: When Task 2's decisions.md report is written, carry this trade-off forward explicitly (not just 'see code comment') so Task 3 (repository) or a later hardening pass can decide whether a stale pending row shown to admins is worth fixing. This is a process note, not a code defect — no action needed in access.go itself.

findings.description: ErrForbidden is declared in costing.go per the task's explicit instruction but is not referenced anywhere in access.go or access_test.go. This is expected and correct for this task's scope (tech-spec assigns 403 handling to RequireAdmin/RequireAccess middleware in a later task), and Go doesn't flag unused package-level vars, so there's no compile or lint issue — flagging only so the next reviewer isn't surprised to grep for ErrForbidden usage and find none yet.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. Confirm in Task 4's (or whichever task adds middleware/handlers) review that ErrForbidden actually gets used somewhere, since right now it's a promise, not a used error.

strengths: Decision 10's has_access||role=='admin' rule is implemented in exactly one function (hasEffectiveAccess) and verified by grep across the whole server tree — no second inline copy of the rule anywhere.

Domain types and interface signatures (Role, AccessState, UserRecord, AccessRequest, UserRepository, AccessRequestRepository) match the tech-spec's Data Models section field-for-field and method-for-method — no drift between spec and delivery.

House style match with costing.go is exact: narrow interfaces, ctx first argument, only domain types cross the service boundary, error wrapping via fmt.Errorf("...: %w", ErrX) throughout, no magic strings (requireLogin centralizes the empty-login check instead of repeating it four times).

CreateRequest's early ErrConflict-without-repo-call path for users who already have access (including via admin role) is tested for both paths explicitly (through flag and through role), matching Decision 10's edge case called out in the task.

The flagged SetAccess/DecideRequest race is handled honestly: documented in-code with the actual trade-off and a concrete pointer to the real fix (repository-level transaction) rather than glossed over, and the design already survived one internal test-design review round that hardened the tests (getCalls assertions) to make the trade-off an enforced invariant rather than an implicit one.

Independently verified, not just read: `go build ./...` clean and `go test ./internal/service/... -v` shows all TestAccessService_* (14 top-level, several with subtables) passing plus the pre-existing TestCostingService_* suite untouched.

SetAccess correctly validates decidedBy as non-empty (attribution can't be silently lost) and requireLogin/requireLogin-equivalent checks run before any repository call is reached, verified by the InvalidArguments test table checking zero repo calls per case.
